text:
Thirteen of Nick Schmaltz's 20 points have come on the power play, which tells you most of what you need to know about his first month. With the extra man he's been close to unstoppable, including the late power-play goal that beat Toronto 3-2 on Tuesday and a three-point night in Montreal on Thursday.

At 5v5 it's a different picture. Utah gets only 44% of the expected goals with him on the ice, 18 points worse than when he sits. From there, two numbers pull in opposite directions. He's shooting 19.6% (nine goals on 6.4 expected), a rate that rarely lasts. Meanwhile his teammates have scored five fewer goals than their chances deserved with him out there, which has cost him assists. Our read: those roughly cancel.

He still ranks 18th of 496 skaters in wins added by his goals, Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 91st percentile in primary shot assists, and Evolving-Hockey put him 26th among 401 forwards last season. Our range lands near 75 points. Watch the 5v5 numbers: that's where his next month gets decided.
headline: Nick Schmaltz is living on the power play
